newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW--Tribune sees '97 EPS up modestly vs '96.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW--Tribune sees '97 EPS up modestly vs '96.

text.p: Tribune Co expects its earnings per share to grow modestly in 1997 over 1996, according to chief financial officer Don Grenesko who cited dilution from a pending broadcasting acquisition.
"We'll be up modestly in 1997 over the earnings per share we're projecting for 1996," Grenesko told Reuters Thursday.

He said 1997 earnings would have been up by a double-digit percentage excluding the effects of its $1.13 billion acquisition of Renaissance Communications Corp, which is expected to be completed in late January or early February.
But dilution from the interest and goodwill amortization associated with the Renaissance deal will reduce expected 1997 earnings by "7.5 to eight percent or so," he added.
He said Tribune's television advertising revenues were "a little bit soft in December," but did not elaborate.
"We're still planning to have a record year in 1996," Grenesko said.

Earlier, Grenesko told an investment conference that Tribune expected to post 1996 earnings slightly below the consensus of $4.23 per share on a primary basis or $3.89 per share diluted. In 1995, it earned 3.55 per diluted share.
He also said 1997 revenues would grow by 12 to 15 percent.
Beyond the Renaissance deal, which will add six television stations, Tribune is looking for further acquisitions in the broadcasting and education markets, Grenesko said.
Tribune is a multimedia company that publishes newspapers and education materials and operates television and radio stations.
Grenesko said Tribune was exploring ways to expand internationally, particularly through acquisitions in the education business where it might add English-as-a-second-language titles.
In publishing, the company said it anticipates revenue growth in the two to four percent range in 1997.

Grenesko said Tribune's growing Internet presence should generate about $15 million in revenues in 1997, up from $2 million this year. This startup business still produces "significant losses," but Grenesko said, "We're putting a lot of effort into it." ((-- Chicago newsdesk 312 408-8787))
